title: Judgment Window Lab: Timing Feel as Two Sliders
subtitle: A timing lab: 20 beats, one shrinking ring, one judgment circle. Drag Perfect Window (40–150ms) and BPM (60–180) sliders to feel where timing feel comes from.

breakdown.title: Rule Skeleton
bullets: 20 notes per round; each hitAt lands exactly on a beat, and the ring spawns 2 beats early from the outer circle
Click error ≤ Perfect window judges Perfect, ≤ Good window (Perfect × 2.2) judges Good, and a note left unclicked past the Good window judges Miss
After all 20 notes resolve: Perfect + Good ≥ 60% (12 notes) clears the round

breakdown.title: Behavior Loop
bullets: Watch the ring shrink toward the judgment circle → click the canvas at the overlap moment → read the Perfect / Good / Miss feedback
Perfect scores 100 + combo × 5 and extends the combo, Good scores a flat 40, Miss resets the combo to zero
Clicks outside the Good window only flash 'Too early / late': no note is consumed and the combo survives, so experimenting costs nothing

breakdown.title: Implementation Notes
bullets: Judgment picks the unjudged note nearest to the click time, against game.time accumulated at a fixed 60fps step — decoupled from render frame rate
Spawn lead time approach = 2 beats scales with BPM, so the ring's visual shrink speed is identical at any BPM; only beat spacing tightens
Perfect window and BPM are exposed as sliders while everything else is hard-coded, keeping each experiment single-variable

codeSnippets.title: Three-tier timing judgment (real code excerpt from the demo)

demo.note: Hit Start, then click the canvas the moment the shrinking ring overlaps the judgment circle. Drag the Perfect Window and BPM sliders on the side to change judgment strictness and beat density in real time; the round settles after 20 notes.
